checks: No eclipse at 2 of 35 covered epochs where the 5.20512 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 367430670 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 5.205118 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The primary eclipse produces a 5.02% dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The transit signal achieved a high detection significance of 340.8 in the BLS periodogram, and pixel-level analysis confirmed the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 54.2, though the centroid offset of 2.6 arcsec warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, analysis reveals that alternating eclipse depths differ significantly, suggesting the true orbital period may be twice the initially measured value - hence the corrected period listed here. This data quality flag indicates an open question about the system's characteristics that should be considered in any further investigation.
